key_insight: Uni-HamGNN is a universal graph neural network that learns spin–orbit-coupled Hamiltonians across the periodic table, enabling rapid, accurate prediction of relativistic electronic structures for materials screening.
problem_solved: First-principles calculations including spin–orbit coupling (SOC) are computationally expensive and scale poorly for high-throughput screening; there is a need for transferable, accurate surrogate models that capture SOC-driven electronic effects across many elements and crystal structures.
method: Physics-informed Hamiltonian representation: encode local atomic environments, symmetry and explicit SOC terms into a Hamiltonian form suitable for learning.
Graph neural network maps atom-centered features and pair interactions to Hamiltonian matrix elements, enforcing physical constraints (Hermiticity, rotational symmetry) for transferability.
Train on diverse DFT+SOC datasets and validate by predicting band structures, gaps, and topological indicators much faster than ab initio methods.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, Uni-HamGNN provides a high-fidelity, fast surrogate for relativistic electronic structure that can be embedded in materials screening and inverse design pipelines, dramatically reducing compute cost and enabling larger, SOC-sensitive search spaces.
